newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain approves new digital television law.
newsitem.headline: Spain approves new digital television law.

text.p: Spain's Congress approved on Thursday a new digital television law requiring digital TV operators to use a new decoder system called multicrypt if in two months no compatibility agreement is reached on the use of the other system, already in use by Canal Satellite Digital.
The law was approved with 170 votes in favour, 133 against and 19 abstentions, a parliamentary spokesman said.

The conservative Popular Party government won the backing of the Basque parliamentary group, and the United Left. The socialists voted against, while Catalonia's Convergence and Union and the Canary Coalition abstained.
Canal Satellite, which is owned 15 percent by Antena 3 and 85 percent by Sogecable, rejected the law in a first reaction.
"This law imposes a technology that doesn't exist and favours an operator that isn't in the market yet," said a Canal Satellite spokesman in a clear reference to Telefonica.
The company added in a statement it intends to file the case before the European Court of Justice in Luxembourg.

At the moment, Canal Satellite is the only digital platform in Spain, while the group headed by Telefonica, which also includes RTVE, Mexican group Televisa and various regional channels and editorial groups, is not yet marketing its services.
Canal Satellite has offered pay television since February. It has 32,000 subscribers and another 26,000 on a waiting list.
